newsitem.title: USA: LME copper backwardation not fundamental - NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: LME copper backwardation not fundamental - NYMEX.

text.p: The current severe backwardation in the futures copper price structure on the London Metal Exchange (LME) has characteristics that are not justified by the supply and demand fundamentals, said Neill Wolkoff, vice president of the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) on Tuesday.
"Looking at comparative data, the data looks troubling in a way similar to what it did before the Sumitomo problems," Wolkoff said at a seminar sponsored by American Metal Market magazine.
Backwardation is when a commodity's immediate delivery prices are higher than prices for deferred delivery.
Copper's cash-to-three months spread on the LME was around $160 a tonne early Tuesday, but had seen highs around $300 a tonne in late January.
"The LME operates within its own rules and governance, and they will have to deal with it," he added.
Wolkoff noted that the COMEX backwardation is only half that being experienced on LME.
Early Tuesday the COMEX February/May spread was trading around 4.80 cents a pound.
"There have been LME warehouse stock increases in the US, as has happened in the past, particularly in the Long Beach warehouse," Wolkoff said.
Total LME copper stocks have recovered more than 20 percent or 35,000 tonnes since the end of January, analysts noted.
"NYMEX will nevertheless look at the backwardation to see if there will be any impact on its (NYMEX) market," Wolkoff said.
